summary: Defines a community-based administrative framework for SNMP version 2, using simple community names for access control as SNMPv1 did. It was an experimental protocol and is now historic.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1901 describes how community-based SNMPv2 identifies the administrative context for a message. It reuses the SNMPv1 community framework and changes the message version value for SNMPv2.

subtitle: SNMPv2's community-based administrative framework and message wrapper.

tldr.problem: SNMP version 2 needed an administrative framework connecting messages with rules for management access.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC reuses the SNMPv1 community-based framework and defines a message wrapper with a version value, community name, and protocol data unit.
tldr.outcome: RFC 1901 is classified as Historic. It is an Experimental memo and states that security issues are not discussed in the document.

today: RFC 1901 is classified as Historic in the supplied metadata and was published as an Experimental memo in January 1996. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The SNMPv2 Framework
sections.content:
RFC 1901 defines a community-based administrative framework for SNMP version 2. SNMPv2 is described across several companion documents and is derived from the earlier SNMPv1 framework.

The RFC points readers to separate documents for management information, textual conventions, conformance statements, protocol operations, transport mappings, and instrumentation.
sections.plainLanguage: SNMPv2 is a collection of specifications for naming managed information, exchanging messages, and describing agent capabilities. This RFC covers how messages use the community-based administrative framework.

sections.title: Parts of the Management System
sections.content:
An SNMP management system has agents with access to management instrumentation, one or more management stations, and a protocol for exchanging information. Managed objects are represented in a Management Information Base (MIB).

The framework around protocol operations defines authentication, authorization, access control, and privacy policies. Other SNMPv2 documents define the data structures and protocol behavior referenced here.
sections.plainLanguage: An agent exposes information about a managed device, and a management station exchanges requests and responses with it. The framework describes the rules around those exchanges.

sections.title: Community-Based Administration
sections.content:
The administrative framework is the same one defined for SNMPv1. It associates each message with a community, and use of this framework with SNMPv2 is commonly called Community-based SNMPv2.

The RFC updates the types of access, requires relevant SNMPv2 statistics to be incremented, and removes the requirement that a response use the same transport address to which the request was sent.
sections.plainLanguage: Each message carries a community name that associates it with the administrative framework. The RFC makes several procedure changes for SNMPv2 while retaining the SNMPv1 framework.

sections.title: The Message Wrapper
sections.content:
The message wrapper contains a version, a community name encoded as an octet string, and data containing the protocol data unit. The version value in this framework is 1, different from the value used in RFC 1157.

The RFC notes that the authorizationError(16) error status is unused with this framework, though it may be used by a future administrative framework.
sections.plainLanguage: An SNMPv2 message has three main parts: a version label, the community name, and the request or response data. The changed version value distinguishes the message format from SNMPv1.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC's Security Considerations section says that security issues are not discussed in this memo.

The document describes a community name in each message but provides no analysis of its security properties.
sections.plainLanguage: The RFC does not analyze the security of the community-based framework. It only describes the community name carried in each message.
